findings.source_quote: οἷον οὐρανός, γῆ, ὕδωρ, ἀὴρ καὶ εἰ ἄλλο τι ἐστὶν σῶμα
findings.english_quote: such as heaven, earth, water, air, or any other body
findings.issue: The Greek expressly includes the existential condition καὶ εἰ ἄλλο τι ἐστὶν σῶμα, “and if there is any other body.” The draft retains the open-ended list but leaves this conditional clause unexpressed.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore the condition, for example: “such as heaven, earth, water, air, and any other body, if there is one”. Preserve the following relative clause and its disclosed interpretive alternatives. The revised sentence requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τοῦτο γὰρ αὐτῷ (τὸ οὐδέν) οἰκειότερον ὄνομα
findings.english_quote: Nothing is a more suitable name for it.
findings.issue: Here τὸ οὐδέν identifies the proposed name, “nothing.” Without quotation marks, the English can instead mean that no name is more suitable, reversing the intended naming claim. The explanatory γὰρ is also unexpressed.
findings.suggested_revision: Use: “For ‘nothing’ is a more suitable name for it.” This clarifies the name being proposed without changing the supplied reading.
